The catalogue this repository publishes, so a consumer gets the language server by name instead of by path: `claude plugin marketplace add ecoma-io/lattice`, then `claude plugin install lattice@lattice`. It is at the repository root rather than under `.claude/`, because a marketplace added from GitHub is read from the default branch's root and a catalogue hidden inside an agent's own config directory would be found by this repository's sessions and by nobody else's.

A session in THIS repository reads it too, which is the arrangement worth naming: the plugin ships from the same commit as the code it acts on, so a change to the server is reviewed in the pull request that makes it, and there is no published version for a session here to be behind.

This file lists what the repository OFFERS. `.claude/settings.json` decides what a session here USES, and the two are deliberately not the same set. `packages/lattice/src/conformance/plugin-catalogue.integration.test.mjs` holds both halves to what they can each be checked against: every entry here against the manifest it points at, and every plugin those settings enable against the marketplace they name.

Claude Code ignores manifest keys it does not know (`claude plugin validate` says so in as many words), which is where this note lives.
